enc.running_locally: Running locally — your prompts and outputs never leave this device

error_hint.config: There's a configuration issue. Check Settings in the dashboard or review your config.toml file.
error_hint.inference_timeout: The request took too long. Try a shorter prompt, reduce the max tokens, or wait for a less busy time.
error_hint.insufficient_capacity: Not enough peers have the shards needed for this model. Try again later as more peers come online, or download the model shards yourself from the Models tab.
error_hint.insufficient_credits: Your credit balance is too low. Earn credits by hosting model shards (happens automatically) or serving inference for other users. Check your balance on the dashboard.
error_hint.insufficient_disk: Not enough disk space. Free up space or increase the storage limit in Settings → Advanced → max_disk_mb.
error_hint.local_only: This one has to be done on the computer that is running SwarmLLM, because it acts on that machine itself. Open the dashboard there and try again — your API key is fine.
error_hint.model_incomplete_in_swarm: Part of this model isn't on any machine that's reachable right now. If a peer just dropped out this may fix itself shortly. Otherwise fetch the model with `swarmllm get-model <name> --all`, or pick a model the dashboard marks as ready.
error_hint.model_not_available: This model isn't available yet. Open the Models tab in the dashboard to browse and download models, or wait for auto-manage to acquire it from the network.
error_hint.no_model_loaded: No model is loaded yet. Go to the dashboard and select a model to download, or connect to more peers so models can be served from the network.
error_hint.peer_not_found: That peer is offline or unreachable. Check your internet connection and try again later.
error_hint.peer_unresponsive: Another computer in the swarm took this request and then stopped answering — it may have gone offline mid-request. Try again: a new request is usually routed to a different machine.
error_hint.pipeline_generic: The route to run this model couldn't be put together. If a peer dropped out this will fix itself — try once more. If it fails the same way again, the model is missing a piece: fetch it with `swarmllm get-model <name> --all`, or pick a model marked as ready in the dashboard.
error_hint.pipeline_missing_layer: Part of this model isn't available — not on this machine, and not on any connected peer. Fetch the whole model with `swarmllm get-model <name> --all`, or wait for more peers to come online.
error_hint.private_mode_unavailable: Private mode keeps your prompts on your own devices, and none of them has all of this model. Either download it here with `swarmllm get-model <name>`, or add the device that has it to your pool. You can also turn private mode off in Settings — but then your prompts can be sent to other people's machines to run.
error_hint.prompt_privacy_unavailable: Prompt privacy keeps your prompt on this machine, which needs the model's first part stored here — and it isn't. Either fetch it with `swarmllm get-model <name>`, or turn prompt privacy off for this model to let the swarm run it. Retrying as-is won't help.
error_hint.provider_auth: Your API key appears to be invalid or revoked. Update it in Settings → Cloud Providers.
error_hint.provider_generic: The cloud provider returned an error. Try again, switch to a different model, or use a local swarm model.
error_hint.provider_quota: Your cloud provider credits may be exhausted or rate-limited. Top up your account on the provider's website, switch to a free-tier provider (DeepSeek, Groq, NVIDIA NIM), or use a local swarm model instead.
error_hint.segment_failover_exhausted: A computer running part of this model failed mid-request, and no other machine was free to take over its part. This is usually momentary — try again, and the swarm will build a fresh route.
error_hint.shard_incomplete: A model file did not download completely and will be fetched again automatically. This usually means the connection dropped part-way.
error_hint.shard_integrity: A model file was corrupted and will be re-downloaded automatically. This is usually caused by an interrupted download — try again in a moment.
error_hint.unauthorized: Authentication required. Your API key can be found on the dashboard Settings page. Include it as a Bearer token in the Authorization header.

hw.cpu_mode_tip:
Inference runs on CPU — responses are slower than GPU.

Models are memory-mapped from disk, so they use much less RAM than their file size. A 5 GB model might only use a few hundred MB of RAM because the OS only loads the parts being actively used.

GPU-enabled nodes handle requests faster and earn more credits.
hw.gpu_mode_tip: Inference running on GPU — fast responses
hw.mode_note_cpu_body: No GPU is used for inference. Instead, shard files are memory-mapped from disk and the OS loads only the bytes that are actively needed, so a 5 GB model may only occupy a few hundred MB of RAM. The contribution bar tracks RAM used by loaded model data, not VRAM.
hw.mode_note_cpu_title: CPU mode — models memory-mapped from disk
hw.mode_note_gpu_body: Model shards are loaded fully into GPU VRAM for fast inference. The contribution bar shows how much of your VRAM is dedicated to hosted shards. System RAM stays low because the GPU holds the weights.
hw.mode_note_gpu_title: GPU mode — shards loaded into VRAM
hw.ram_tip_cpu: In CPU mode, models are memory-mapped from disk. Only the parts being actively used are loaded into RAM, so a 5 GB model may only use a few hundred MB. The OS manages this automatically.
hw.ram_tip_gpu: Models are loaded into GPU VRAM for fast inference. RAM usage is low.
hw.vram_idle_tip:
GPU is not used for inference in CPU mode.

Models are memory-mapped from disk into RAM instead. This is slower than GPU but uses much less memory — the OS only loads the parts being actively used, so a 5 GB model may only use a few hundred MB.

This bar shows GPU driver memory only (baseline allocation).
hw.vram_live_only_tip: {used} in use on the GPU right now (measured live).
hw.vram_live_tip:
{used} in use on the GPU right now (measured live).

Loaded models are budgeted at about {committed}, but a model only uses memory while it is actually running — so live usage is normally well below that.

The file stays on disk. The model worker will restart without this shard. Active inference may be briefly interrupted.
